text: This specification defines the WOFF2 font packaging format. This format was designed to provide a reasonably easy-to-implement compression of font data with significantly better compression than previous techniques, suitable for use with CSS @font-face rules.

The experiments conducted as part of WOFF2 development and evaluation have shown that Brotli compression technology works more efficiently and produces better compression gains for WOFF2 fonts if the CFF outline data is de-subroutinized prior to WOFF2 encoding - this will on average reduce the compressed data size by 5-10%.

A transform can be applied to three types of tables: glyf, representing outline data, loca, representing the offsets of the individual glyphs within a glyf table, and hmtx, representing glyph horizontal metrics, if these tables are present in a font.
To begin supporting Japanese, we gathered character frequency data from millions of Japanese webpages and analyzed them to inform how to slice the fonts.
For Japanese, we found that segmenting the first 3,000 characters into 20 slices was best, resulting in clients downloading 80% fewer bytes than they would if we just sent the whole font.

The core features we rely on to efficiently deliver sliced fonts are unicode-range and woff2. Browsers that support unicode-range and woff2 also support HTTP/2. HTTP/2 enables the concurrent delivery of many small files.

This specification defines a method to incrementally transfer a font from server to client. The client loads only the portion(s) of the font that they actually need, significantly reducing data transfer.
Incremental font transfer does not suffer from this issue as it can encompass the original font and all of it's layout rules.

Web fonts for languages with large character sets-such as Chinese, Japanese, and Korean (CJK)-often exceed several megabytes in size. Downloading these massive files significantly delays text rendering, consumes excessive bandwidth, and degrades the user experience.
From our demo, incremental font transfer sees typical savings of 50% or more compared to the subsetting approach.

Patch Subset shows the largest reduction in bytes transferred (a median improvement of 90% on all but the slowest networks, dropping to 65% on 2G). Unicode Range had a consistent but modest reduction, (a median improvement of 50%) on all networks.

The TrueType or OpenType fonts used for CJK languages had a median size of 1,834,496 bytes, with a spread from 16,832 bytes (5th percentile) to 5,524,208 bytes (95th percentile). The median size once WOFF2 compressed was 768,492 bytes.

It became clear from both trials that network bandwidth, although important, was not the limiting factor for performance. Rather, the network latency (overall round-trip time for a single request) was the important variable.
A 2019 study by the HTTP Archive found that the median number of bytes used for Web Fonts on websites in China was zero.
This works particularly well for Chinese, Japanese, and Korean fonts, where 90% or more of the font data is outline data.

In addition to the parts listed above (prefix code for insert-and-copy lengths, literals, distances, block types, block counts, and the context map), the meta-block header contains the number of uncompressed bytes coded in the meta-block and two additional parameters used in the representation of match distances.
Combined, they are reducing the size of the downloaded fonts by more than 40 percent on average.

Across five Google Noto fonts (LGC, KR, JP, TC, SC), MLFont cuts 3G per-glyph latency by 56.7%-75.3% over single-file delivery and 46.1%-66.3% over equal-bin baselines on CJK with 100% coverage, reduces CSS intervals by 17.9%-41.7%, and achieves 1.56x-6.09x cold-cache speedups (65.4%-84.9% CJK and 44.7% LGC bandwidth savings) across 2020 websites in simulator and Headless Chrome benchmarks.

If a slice groups together characters that rarely co-occur on the same web page, downloading it for a single needed character forces the client to download hundreds of unused glyphs, resulting in poor glyph utilization.
Fonts accounted for 139 KB on home pages and 138 KB on inner pages.
A revolutionary font subetter that supports CJK and any characters! It enables multi-threaded subset of otf, ttf, and woff2 fonts, allowing for precise control over package size.
The dynamic subsetting watches for any change to the Document Object Model (DOM)-such as a news feed or a comments section-and then requests any new characters that need to be added to the subset.
WOFF 2.0 responses use ~25 percent less bytes than WOFF with Zopfli.

日本語のウェブフォントはグリフ数が多く、ファイルサイズが大きいため、初回表示の遅延と通信量の増加の原因となっています。本調査では、実測した12種類のCJKフォント、44サイトの実ページ、グーグルの実際のフォントスライス分け、およびW3Cの仕様や研究論文をもとに、各圧縮・配信手法の効果を定量的に比較しました。その結果、頻度上位の数百文字を1枚にまとめた共有ベーススライス、ページ本文と完全一致の厳密サブセット、不足グリフを差分で足す増分フォント転送（IFT）の3層構成が、キャッシュ再利用性と欠落グリフがないことを維持しながら、1ページあたり110KiB程度まで転送量を削減できることを示しました。ページごとに厳密サブセットを生成する場合とバイト数がほぼ同じでも、前者は全ページ・全サイトでキャッシュを共有できることを示しました。また、共有圧縮辞書ではCJKの輪郭が圧縮率 0〜0.4%しか改善しないこと、可変フォントが静的インスタンスの約2倍大きいことを実測しました。本レポートには測定手順、再現用スクリプト、および実測値をまとめた資料を収録しています。
For greater compression effectiveness, the glyf table is split into several substreams, to group like data together.

The WOFF 2.0 transformations applied to certain tables are designed to reduce and/or eliminate the built-in redundancies of the SFNT format and restructure the font data stream for more efficient entropy encoding. As a result, the reconstructed font data will retain the exact functionality of the input font file.
The modified transformation is based on a similar transformation described in MicroType Express specification.

It is possible that depending on the context and on the level of optimizations being applied to reconstructed glyf table data, the size of the reconstructed table may be greater than, less than, or equal to the original size of the glyf table of the input font compressed by WOFF2.

本レポートでは、WOFF2を超える新しいCJKフォント圧縮手法「GLC(Glyph-Level Compression)」を提案し、実測で検証した。GLCは、WOFF2の出力形式を変えずに、ビルド時に4つの前処理を追加する。(1)CFFフォントをglyf(二次ベジェ)に変換してWOFF2の内容依存変換を適用可能にする、(2)CFFのサブルーチンを展開してから圧縮する、(3)縦書き用メトリクスを削除する、(4)座標を指定格子へ量子化する。実測では、Noto Sans JPの静的400重み全体(17,936グリフ)のWOFF2が2.303 MBから、誤差0.2% emの量子化で1.921 MB(-16.6%)、0.4% emで1.667 MB(-27.6%)、0.8% emで1.429 MB(-37.9%)になった。3,000文字の部分集合では、Noto Sans JP -13.2/-23.2/-32.7%、M PLUS 1p -8.4/-17.9/-27.3%、Zen Kaku Gothic New -11.5/-22.1/-32.4%、CFFのSource Han Sans JPは変換と量子化を組み合わせて -26.6/-35.1/-42.4%であった。品質はFreeType(ヒンティングなし)で画素差0.03〜0.36%であり、輪郭の幾何誤差は最大でも格子幅の半分(0.2〜0.8% em)に収まる。提案手法には「変換前後を両方エンコードして小さい方を採用する」安全弁を必ず組み込むべきである。実際、韓国のNanum Gothicでは4単位量子化で 오히려7.0%大きくなった。
